https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/08/20/navr.text: Menü Kereső Párbeszédet indít Magyarország dolgairól Navracsics Tibor és a volt űrbiztos, Ferencz Orsolya Belföld Bánáti Anna Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Párbeszédet indítana Magyarország jövőjéről és múltjáról Navracsics Tibor, a Fidesz korábbi közigazgatási és területfejlesztési minisztere mindezt Facebook-videóban jelentette be augusztus 20-án. A videóban a volt miniszter arról beszél, hogy „két oldal helyett egyenes út kell”, mert Magyarország eljutott abba a helyzetbe, amikor „két oldal végletes, végzetes szembenállása az ország egységét rombolja, cselekvőképességét rontja”. Ezért párbeszédre van szükség, ami felülírja a két oldal szembenállását. „Az elmúlt időszak azt bizonyította, hogy a politikai bosszú, a másik kiátkozása, kirekesztése a közösségből sehova sem vezet, de biztosan nem a jövő felé vezető út.” Navracsics ezért olyan társadalmi kezdeményezést indít a „polgári demokraták” nevében, ami ígérete szerint párthovatartozástól függetlenül mindenkit hív, hogy beszélgessen az ország jövőjéről és az elmúlt 100 nap, 16 év és 36 év tanulságairól. Hogy Navracsics pontosan milyen platformon képzeli el a párbeszédet, nem derül ki, mint ahogy az sem, kikkel képzeli el az „egyenes út” építését. A videóban a volt miniszter mellett egy ponton megjelenik Ferencz Orsolya egykori űrbiztos, a Fidesz volt országgyűlési képviselője is, aki nemrég arról beszélt, a kormányoldal elmulasztotta az érdemi megújulást . Az erről szóló bejegyzést Navracsics is megosztotta, azzal a kommentárral, hogy „Ferencz Orsolya most is pontosan fogalmazott”. Navracsics egy hónappal ezelőtt a Telexnek arról beszélt Tusványoson , hogy rendszeresen beszélget Orbán Viktorral, és azt reméli, van lehetősége befolyásolni a Fidesz irányát, viszont úgy látja, hogy a megújulás csak a pártot évtizedek óta irányító Orbánnal lehetséges. By Tom McArthur Â and Â Bethany Bell ,Â Reporting from in Bavaria Published 30 August 2026, 11:39 BST Updated 4 hours ago A British woman has died after being stabbed at a railway station in southern Germany in the early hours of Sunday morning, police have said. The 31-year-old woman was attacked at the station in Rosenheim, Bavaria, shortly before 01:00 local time (00:00 BST). She was taken to hospital where she died as a result of "severe" injuries, the Bavarian Police said in a statement. Officers arrested a 27-year-old German man at the scene immediately after the incident. The background and motive for the attack is under investigation, the statement added. Police have asked anyone who may have witnessed "an argument or physical altercation" at the station late on Saturday or early on Sunday to contact them. The suspect, from the FÃ¼rstenfeldbruck district, will be brought before magistrates later on Sunday, according to German news agency DPA. It is unclear whether the two knew each other or what the woman was doing in Bavaria, DPA also reported. Rosenheim is one of the largest cities in Upper Bavaria and is a busy rail hub for passengers travelling to Austrian cities including Vienna, Salzburg and Innsbruck. The Rosenheimer Herbstfest - an event similar to the Oktoberfest beer festival - is currently taking place in the area. Responding to the attack, Rosenheim Mayor Abuzar Erdogan said "there are no indications of a security threat in our city or of any link to our Herbstfest". "The criminal investigation department is working closely with the public prosecutor's office to investigate the circumstances and motive behind the crime as a matter of urgency," he wrote in a statement. A Foreign Office spokesperson told the BBC: "We are supporting the family of a British woman who died in Germany [and] are in touch with the local authorities." The AfD’s win in the Saxony-Anhalt election in eastern Germany, with 43.8 percent of the vote, is as much a major moment for the other nations of NATO as it is for the country where the elections took place. And Poland in particular. The strongest election result for a far-right party in Germany since World War II comes with the rise of fears of Russian sabotage and hybrid warfare across Europe—including recent attacks on Leipzig/Halle Airport in eastern Germany, and fires in factories in Estonia and Poland. Germany’s turn to the right may well spell danger for a bloc desperate to defend itself against Vladimir Putin , and protect Ukraine. The AfD will not only weaken Germany, but is also pro- Russia , with its leader Alice Weidel, suggesting that Germany end its boycott of Russian oil and gas. Germany currently hosts NATO’s critical centers such as the Headquarters Allied Air Command in Ramstein, responsible for conducting air operations, as well as the Grafenwoehr Training Area, the largest U.S. military training facility in Europe. Nonetheless, with an AfD victory, it may be harder for NATO to work as a bloc to defend the continent against Russia. Read More on Opinion Amid existing debates about NATO’s spending—Germany, according to NATO estimates, will spend only 2.69 percent of its GDP on defense in 2026—the country’s new, disruptive politics will weaken a once essential player in NATO further. Germany is now finally increasing its defense budget as a result of Russian threats, with plans to double this in four years. But it is a country to its east—Poland—which is rapidly turning into the sparkly new weapon in NATO’s arsenal. It is becoming the operational, and military powerhouse of NATO’s eastern flank—and, potentially, more important than Germany itself to NATO. Experts are claiming that while Germany remains NATO’s logistical hub, Poland is becoming strategically significant for its forward capabilities. With Russia on its doorstep , and a history of invasion and conflict from its larger neighbor, Poland has in fact been one of the champions of NATO’s aim to spend 5 percent of GDP on defense—even calling on countries to surpass NATO’s target, and achieve 5 percent as early as 2030. Though Germany has up until recently focused on military restraint, Poland has been investing in defense for years against a Russia the West too easily ignored pre-2022. Poland is now one of the leading centers for military strength in NATO, with an estimated 4.68 percent of its GDP, $53.8 billion, spent on defense in 2026—almost double that of Germany. It is also aiming to build the largest land army in Europe, with its armed forces consisting of over 220,000 personnel this year. Poland is also heavily investing in military technology , including South Korean K2 Black Panther tanks, with plans to operate 1,100 tanks in total, more than Germany , France, the U.K. and Italy combined, by 2030. Poland has also been investing in civilian defense, with the "W Gotowości" (Always Ready) program promoting civilian military training, first aid, and cybersecurity, strengthening its overall security. Another scheme launched recently was "What the Fejk": a teaching program for students aged 10-19 to help them spot deepfakes by creating their own. Vitally, Poland is also taking measures to improve domestic defense production, with half its orders now going to domestic producers, and 30.4 billion złotys ($8.15 billion) spent last year on domestic and central European-based defense. Some technologies are even attracting NATO allies, including its Piorun air-defense systems, which have recently been purchased by Norway, Lithuania and Latvia. Previously, Belgium, Estonia and Sweden have bought Pioruns—alongside the United States, which ordered several hundred in 2022. Related Story The New ‘Muslim NATO’ Faces First Major Test Poland has also been essential to Ukraine as a vital front-line hub for Ukrainian military and humanitarian aid. Its Rzeszów-Jasionka airport in the east of the country is home to the NATO Security Assistance and Training for Ukraine logistical hub, which manages 18,000 tons of material per month. Meanwhile, Poland is also deepening its relationship with the U.S. through the thousands of U.S. troops hosted on Polish soil—including the announcement of an additional 5,000 troops to Poland in May, and plans by the Polish government to allow a new permanent U.S. military base in Poland. Recently, Poland was the first NATO ally to undertake training developed for the Green Berets, the elite U.S. Army special forces. Based on and simulating Ukrainian battlefields , the training involved drone warfare and travel over enemy lines. Poland is now turning into a bridge between America and Europe’s eastern flank, as an essential security partner, a military hub, and a regional network. While Germany is now rebuilding militarily, and remains Europe’s economic giant, this is after decades of underinvestment—Poland is building its military around the assumption that the old world has failed. And Germany’s huge industrial base does not automatically translate into military capability: the collapse of the Franco-German future combat air system is a case in point. As it stands, the country that is closest to the threat is increasingly the one shaping NATO’s strategy. Juliette Bretan teaches at the Faculty of English at Cambridge University and previously worked as a research assistant for the Centre for Geopolitics at Cambridge. https://www.teamtalk.com/liverpool/alex-.text: Liverpool Premier League • England Official Club Website www.liverpoolfc.com Bournemouth star Alex Scott is a top target for Chelsea and Liverpool Liverpool 5th • EPL News Fixtures Results Squad Stats Fabrizio Romano has verified what it will take for Liverpool to sign Alex Scott in January, though Chelsea are providing stiff competition. Liverpool waved goodbye to a midfielder over the summer when selling Curtis Jones to Inter Milan. The Reds chosen not to sign a direct replacement, instead placing their trust in Trey Nyoni who’s seen a surge in game-time. However, the brutal truth is Liverpool essentially have four players for two spots, and for a club competing on four fronts, that’s not enough. Wataru Endo and James McConnell aren’t of the standard Liverpool require, meaning Andoni Iraola can only realistically select from Alexis Mac Allister, Ryan Gravenberch, Dominik Szoboszlai and Nyoni. Gravenberch missed Liverpool’s victory over Brentford on Saturday through suspension. It is perhaps for that reason that the Reds rushed Szoboszlai back into the starting eleven after recovering from a minor hamstring injury. However, the Hungarian pulled up after half an hour with a recurrence of the issue, and Iraola has since confirmed he’ll be out of action for some time. Dominik Szoboszlai re-injures his hamstring Iraola said : “Dom felt the same injury, it’s not a new injury and was probably not healed enough, so we will need more time with him. Jeremie Frimpong’s was new, I think he finished cramping the other day [against LASK]. “I put him on because playing against 10 [men], going forward I thought he could give us more than Ronald [Araujo]. After, I value a lot and he was very good, Victor [Munoz] playing as a right-back. “But it will mean we will lose Dom and Jeremie for some time, yes.” The past week perfectly sums up why clubs competing in multiple competitions require excellent strength in depth. With Liverpool reluctant to throw Nyoni in at the deep end, too much will be asked of Mac Allister, Gravenberch and Szoboszlai this season, and it seems almost inevitable the players will break down. Accordingly, Liverpool are ready to rectify the perilous midfield predicament in January, with the BBC and Fabrizio Romano both confirming they’re interest in signing Alex Scott . TEAMtalk understands Chelsea believe they’re the frontrunners for the 23-year-old’s signature , though we’ve also been told Liverpool cannot be discounted. And on Saturday evening, transfer guru, Fabrizio Romano, took to YouTube to provide his take on Scott’s future, with Bournemouth now giving a mammoth January sale the green light. Liverpool learn conditions to sign Alex Scott Romano declared: “Save the name I told you already on YouTube a few weeks ago and I’m maintaining of Alex Scott for 2027. “Because after a number of meetings, not only one, a number of meetings between his agents and Bournemouth. the decision of the club is to change their stance in the January transfer window. “So in the summer, Chelsea tried twice to sign Alex Scott. Arsenal called before signing Bruno Guimaraes. Liverpool called to understand the situation without sending any bid. So all the English top clubs trying to understand the situation. “Chelsea were the more aggressive and Bournemouth told all these clubs the player is not for sale. The player is going nowhere. “Then they wanted Alex Scott to sign a new contract but there was no agreement. Now Bournemouth are open to selling Alex Scott already in the January window. “So Scott leaving in January is a genuine and serious possibility. Then again this depends on the proposal. “Sources close to Bournemouth believe it has to be minimum 100 million pounds. So has to be big money in order to open doors. “It’s not, let me clarify, that Bournemouth are putting the player up for sale in the January window. It’s that Bournemouth could be open to selling if the bid is a good bid, an important bid, and if the player wants to go. So these have to be the conditions. So Chelsea are maintaining a genuine interest in Alex Scott. He’s a player that they are absolutely maintaining on their shortlist. “Then there will be for sure more clubs interested. For example, again I keep mentioning Liverpool. Arsenal invested on Bruno Guimaraes in the summer and they’re super happy with their player. “Let’s see what’s going to happen with Liverpool in midfield. They sold Curtis Jones in the summer transfer window to winter, but they didn’t sign any other midfielder. “So we have to track and follow the situation of Alex Scott with Chelsea being very interested and in regular contact with people close to the player.
